label: text
text: Cargo Moves Freely at Wuchow.

label: text
text: SURTAX NOT COLLECTED.

label: text
text: First Shipment of Tea Arrives in

label: text
text: From latest advices from Wuchow it would appear that no restrictions now exist in that important centre of export of Chinese merchandise. Indeed, our information is that not even the 2½ per cent. surtax on exports has been collected on any shipment leaving Wuchow for Hong Kong to-day.

label: text
text: A telegram of yesterday's date, advising shipment to a large firm of merchants in Hong Kong, reads as follows:—

label: text
text: "Cargo shipped freely this afternoon, our shipment leaves to-morrow."

label: text
text: We are further informed that the first shipment of tea from Canton to Hong Kong for export abroad arrived yesterday afternoon by the s.s. "Kwong Sai". On this shipment the Canton authorities levied the 2½ per cent. surtax.

label: text
text: This is an indication that cargoes are now moving out of Canton with perfect freedom.

label: text
text: News from Kongmoon is not so bad as appeared yesterday when it became known that 60 packages of cargo from Hong Kong had been returned here as consignees were unable to take delivery from ship.

label: text
text: The report about the 40 cases of perfumes and the 20 cases of apples was published in the "China" Mail yesterday.

label: text
text: It is now learned that the merchants there were told—either by members of the Strike movement, or by local authorities—that cargo from Hong Kong could not be landed yet as a depot had not been organised to collect the surtaxes.

label: text
text: Accordingly, the consignees made arrangements for the shipments to be reshipped back to Hong Kong.

label: text
text: Chinese merchants are being told there that Canton is sending the complete equipment, and the personnel to start a local depot, after which merchandise can be landed or shipped.

label: text
text:
Good News for Housekeepers.
No material change has occurred in the situation. In spite of malicious rumours, confidence is still gaining. One such rumour was that 100 passengers down from Canton on one boat had been arrested here by the Police. There is, needless to say, no truth whatever in this.

label: text
text: Steamboats and steamers are running to schedule but it is felt that cargo will be restricted until the attitude of the Nationalist Government with regard to collection of taxes, becomes more defined.

label: text
text: Another encouraging feature was the shipment of silk piece-goods down here this week.

label: text
text: Communications with Wuchow and other up-country ports have resulted in immediate improvement in the food supply of the Colony, and prices of livestock, poultry and produce should soon have reached pre-strike levels.

label: paragraph_title
text: NEW MINISTRIES.

label: text
text: IMPROVE THE NATIONALIST" GOVERNMENT:

label: text
text: CANTON CONFERENCE

label: text
text: One of the proposals submitted by the Presiding Committee to the joint Kuomintang Conference in Canton was:

label: text
text: Among the Committee of the Nationalist Government, three should be two members at least for each province, who can represent the members in the various provinces now under the control of the Nationalist Government.

label: text
text: Besides the Ministries of Foreign Affairs, and Finance, which are necessarily required, two additional Ministries (Military Affairs, and Communications) may be instituted by the Nationalist Government according to the extent to which military affairs and communications may be developed. The Judicial Administrative Committee should be converted into a Ministry, while the Military Council should remain as at present without any change.

label: text
text: The above were carefully considered by the various delegates at the Conference, and were afterwards unanimously passed.

label: paragraph_title
text: RUNAWAY CHICKEN.

label: paragraph_title
text: COOLIE WHO OUTWITTED HIS FELLOWS.

label: text
text: CAUGHT BIRD FIRST.

label: text
text: An amusing story was related before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning by a Chinese coolie who was charged with unlawful possession of a chicken.

label: text
text: Defendant said that the fowl "broke away from a verandah" and he saw six or seven persons chasing it. He joined in the chase and caught the bird first. Further that it was his intention to make a present of it to his wife.

label: text
text: His Worship: So you were the lucky one, or at the moment you thought you were lucky. But it was not your chicken?

label: text
text: Defendant admitted this was so, but said he was prepared to surrender the chicken if anybody had claimed it.

label: text
text: Divisional-Inspector Grant stated that defendant was found by a detective with the chicken under his arm and, when questioned gave the same story about the bird having flown down from a verandah. Defendant pointed out the verandah of the house, but none of the inmates claimed the bird.

label: text
text: In imposing a fine of $5, or seven days' imprisonment, His Worship advised defendant to leave chickens alone in future.

text: MIDNIGHT MURDER.

label: paragraph_title
text: SHAUKIWAN ASSAILANT IN COURT.

label: text
text: POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

label: text
text: As a sequel to the death of a carpenter and the wounding of another man when a Chinese armed with an axe ran amok shortly after midnight yesterday at Shauklwan, the alleged assailant, Mok Choi, was brought before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning and formally charged with murder.

label: text
text: To a question by His Worship as to whether there was another defendant in the case, Divisional Inspector Clark said that he had not quite got to the bottom of the affair and was still carrying out his investigations.

label: text
text: Defendant was formally remanded for the one week.

label: paragraph_title
text: STRIKERS TROUBLE.

label: paragraph_title
text: Dissatisfied With Their Leaders.

label: text
text: MORE CROSS-EXAMINATION

label: text
text: Armed Pickets Arrest Members of

label: text
text: Dissent is reported to have broken out in the strikers' camp at Canton, leading to the arrest by armed pickets of eight men alleged to be members of a "dissatisfied" union.

label: text
text: There is much behind the scenes that baffles investigation. Vernacular papers in Canton have little or nothing to say on the matter. The printers and compositors' union is stated to have received instructions that the newspapers are not to insert any article referring to discontent among the strikers.

label: text
text: The number of malcontents is growing. Delegates on the Strike Executive are said to have been “cross-examined” time and again as to “why the manifesto was issued, calling off the “strike”.

label: paragraph_title
text: Leaders Accused.

label: text
text: Some have even gone as far—says the report—to accuse a few of the leaders of ulterior motives in “voluntarily calling off the strike.”

label: text
text: In the circumstances, it is not surprising that rumours are current, hinting that a portion of the rank and file has made ugly threats against those in power in labour circles.

label: text
text: Conditions similar to martial law are reported to have been imposed at Tung Yuen, the strike headquarters in the east suburb of Canton.

label: text
text: Discontented strikers have ignored the gratuity of $10 (as the first instalment of the bonus of $100) and their attitude portends open disobedience of their elected leaders.

label: paragraph_title
text: Possible Break-up.

label: text
text: The report goes on to say that only those on important business are permitted to approach the working committees of the Strike movement.

label: text
text:
A feeling of uneasiness pre-
vails.

label: text
text: Members of one labour union in the city were suspected of dangerous motives. From 30 to 40 pickets, fully armed, proceeded to this union, under orders from the Strike Committee, and arrested eight men in the Union.

label: text
text: It is felt that this dissent among the strikers may have the effect of leading towards the movement breaking up, through secession and other causes, but possibilities exist of trouble in the ranks.
